newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clal Israel CEO to step down.
newsitem.headline: Clal Israel CEO to step down.

text.p: David Wainshal, the president and chief executive of Clal Israel Ltd, one of the country's leading conglomerates, said on Tuesday he would resign as soon as a replacement could be found.
In a letter to IDB Holding Corp, the biggest shareholder of Clal, Wainshal said he was assuming that a replacement would be found by March 1997, when he would have completed six years in his post.
Wainshal, 61, had originally requested to step down last March but was asked to stay on to complete an important phase of the company's restructuring.
A few months ago Wainshal restated his intention but agreed to remain until March 1997, when the 1996 financial results will be published.
IDB, another major holding concern, owns 49.4 percent of Clal, directly and through its subsidiary Discount Investment . Bank Hapoalim owns 25 percent of Clal.

"Mr. Wainshal fulfilled his job with great ability and success and with our full support. We have complete confidence in him and regret his decision to resign," Eli Cohen, managing director of IDB, said in a statement.
Cohen noted that before taking over at Clal Wainshal held various positions within the IDB group and IDB intends to offer him other posts now.
A spokesman for IDB refused to comment on candidates to succeed Wainshal.
The Clal group's 1995 aggregate turnover exceeded $5 billion, of which over $1.4 billion was derived from direct exports.
